name: Archaeological Site of Cyrene
description: Cyrene is an ancient Greek city in northeastern Libya, founded around the late seventh century BC by settlers from the island of Thera (Santorini). It sits on a ridge in the Jebel Akhdar uplands, where temples, theatres, bathhouses and colonnaded halls spread across several hectares. Rich from horses and the medicinal plant silphium, it later became a Roman city and thrived until the earthquake of 365.
